title: Cash-investment liquidity ladder
prompt:
Construct the highest-income permitted investment ladder without compromising operating liquidity.

Begin with the July liquidity, banking, and covenant-outlook thread in `Requests/`, including the bank follow-up. Use the current controller-tied workpapers and operating extracts, keeping earlier versions only for comparison. Resolve conflicts using dates, approvals, document status, and management correspondence. Reconcile posted Alder Ridge balances through the contractor-accounting MCP; keep external targets, peer data, bank terms, and market evidence tied to their controlling finance sources.

Allocate the entire investable balance in approved denominations, observing instrument caps and the commercial-paper concentration limit. Treat the dated cash-need rows as incremental tranches and sum them through each date, test same-day liquidity using settlement eligibility and value factors, satisfy every cumulative requirement, and maximize expected income over the common 100-day horizon under the approved same-yield reinvestment convention.

Do not modify files or post transactions. Also optimize the final executable ladder under weighted-maturity, issuer-concentration, and stressed day-35 liquidity constraints as well as the ordinary cash needs; reoptimize if the ordinary-only optimum fails stress.

Return only one JSON object with exactly these keys: `operating_deposit_allocation`, `government_mmf_allocation`, `four_week_t_bill_allocation`, `eight_week_t_bill_allocation`, `thirteen_week_t_bill_allocation`, `commercial_paper_allocation`, `expected_holding_period_income`, `same_day_liquidity`, `weighted_average_yield`, `commercial_paper_concentration`, `unallocated_cash`, `weighted_average_maturity_days`, `government_issuer_concentration`, `stressed_day_35_liquidity`, `stressed_day_35_liquidity_headroom`, `stress_policy_breaches`, `ladder_executable_after_stress`. Use dollars to two decimals, ratios and percentages as decimal ratios to at least four decimals, and lists as JSON arrays.
